audit_target.branch_note: nextjs-pwa resolves to the identical commit 67b12f7, so the audited source is the same on either branch. Prior superseded accessibility work is at 733909f on branch monorepo-version.
audit_target.app_type: client-rendered hash-view SPA (#view=<key>), Next.js 16.3.6, Tailwind v4, Radix UI

automated_checks: eslint.config.mjs extended with 21 jsx-a11y rules at warning level
next build, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint
method.certification_disclaimer: This is not an accessibility certification. No AT, user, device or browser-execution testing was performed. Claims rest on computed contrast values, source-level assertions and code review.

severity_scale.critical: Blocks a task outright for a user group, or a safety/security-relevant failure.
severity_scale.high: A WCAG A/AA failure that meaningfully obstructs a task; workaround exists but is painful.
severity_scale.medium: A WCAG AA failure or usability defect that degrades but does not block; affects a substantial user group.
severity_scale.low: Minor usability or polish issue; affects few users or little of the task.
severity_scale.informational: No user impact; tooling, process or documentation note.

confidence_scale.high: Computed directly or asserted from source.
confidence_scale.medium: Reasoned from source but dependent on runtime/browser behaviour that was not executed.

lint.warning_detail: 1 pre-existing react-hooks/incompatible-library in login-view.tsx; 2 = UXA-018 (open, owner's in-flight file)

build.exit_code_note: Exit 1 is caused solely by the build script chaining `cp -r ...`, which does not exist on Windows. Pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to compilation and unchanged by this work.

types.detail: src/components/ui/carousel.tsx (x2) and examples/websocket/server.ts (x1) — none modified by this audit. next.config.ts sets typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true.

baseline.method: A throwaway git worktree was created at 67b12f7, the current guard was copied into it and run there, so baseline and post-fix figures come from the same script against the same compiled palette. The worktree was removed afterwards.
baseline.earlier_figure_note: An earlier recorded baseline of 33 came from the pre-extension revision of the guard (10 static guards), and an even earlier one (31) from a weaker revision still. 36 is the reproducible number with the current 70-check guard.

findings.title: Light --primary used as text but only tuned as a fill (4.22-4.42:1)
findings.evidence: Guard section 1: link/active nav 4.22, primary on card 4.42, sidebar active link 4.25, primary button label 4.23 — all below 4.5.
findings.root_cause: One token served two opposing roles: consumed as text for links, active nav, state chips and the scan caption, but tuned only as a fill.
findings.fix: oklch(0.558 0.144 163.5) -> oklch(0.5305 0.144 163.5), the lightest value that passes as text and still passes with --primary-foreground over it as a fill. Applied to all 5 occurrences including ::selection.

findings.title: Focus indicator drawn at 50% opacity (1.97:1 light / 2.67:1 dark)
findings.evidence: ring-ring/50 and outline-ring/50 present in 19 files. A 50% alpha ring composites against the page background and cannot reach 3:1 without driving the token near-black, which would break it as light-theme text.
findings.root_cause: Dimmed ring alpha copied through the UI kit; the same pattern was in the base outline style in globals.css.
findings.fix: Full-strength ring-ring / outline-ring everywhere, including the base outline-ring/50 in globals.css.
findings.verification: Guard section 1 derives the rendered alpha from source, so reintroducing any alpha re-fails the numeric check; SG-04 greps for (ring|outline)-ring/\d+.
findings.note: A prior one-off audit in this repo reported 11 contrast failures including 'muted text 2.23:1'. That script never linearised sRGB; the true value is 5.23:1. Those failures were false.

findings.title: Form-control boundary below 3:1 (1.28-1.40:1)
findings.evidence: Guard section 1: light 1.28 (background) / 1.34 (card), dark 1.40 / 1.33 against a 3:1 requirement — the extent of the control was not perceivable.
findings.root_cause: --input derived from a decorative border colour rather than a perceivable-boundary colour.
findings.fix: Light --input oklch(0.6375 0.008 165); dark --input oklch(0.985 0 0 / 38%). Both sit deliberately just above the floor so borders stay visually quiet.

findings.title: --destructive-foreground was never defined in either theme
findings.evidence: Guard reported MISSING-TOKEN for 'destructive button label' in light and dark. toast.tsx already referenced text-destructive-foreground. The destructive button variant worked around it with a magic dark:bg-destructive/60, which itself failed contrast.
findings.root_cause: Token referenced by components but never added to the @theme mapping or either theme block.
findings.fix: Added --color-destructive-foreground to @theme plus light and dark values; destructive button and badge now use text-destructive-foreground with solid bg-destructive, matching the existing --primary-foreground pattern. Removed dark:bg-destructive/60 and the dimmed ring-destructive/20|/40.

findings.title: White label on emerald action buttons (3.73:1)
findings.evidence: Guard section 2: white on emerald-600 = 3.73 against a 4.5 requirement, on reorder suggestion actions and the install banner.
findings.root_cause: Hard-coded Tailwind utility bypassing the token system, chosen for the fill rather than for its label.
findings.fix: bg-emerald-600 -> bg-emerald-700 (hover emerald-800). bg-primary was considered and rejected to preserve the distinct 'positive action' semantics.
findings.verification: scripts/audit-a11y.mjs section 2, pattern re-asserted against source before measuring

findings.title: White label on amber action buttons (3.20:1)
findings.evidence: Guard section 2: white on amber-600 = 3.20 against a 4.5 requirement, on delivery actions.
findings.root_cause: Hard-coded Tailwind utility bypassing the token system.
findings.fix: bg-amber-600 -> bg-amber-700 (hover amber-800).

findings.title: Scan FAB gradient nearly invisible (1.81:1 vs page, 1.90:1 white icon)
findings.evidence: Guard section 2: to-teal-400 stop 1.81 vs background, white icon 1.90 vs that stop, from-emerald-600 2.69 vs background — all below 3:1. The elevated Scan action is the primary mobile workflow.
findings.root_cause: Gradient stops chosen for visual appeal against a mid-tone surface, not for contrast against the page background they actually sit on.
findings.fix: Gradient from-emerald-700 to-teal-600; SCAN caption switched from emerald-600/dark:emerald-400 to text-primary.

findings.title: Page zoom disabled via viewport metadata
findings.evidence: SG-01 failed at baseline: maximumScale: 1 and userScalable: false present in src/app/layout.tsx, preventing pinch/browser zoom outright.
findings.root_cause: Viewport locked to prevent mobile layout reflow during pinch zoom.
findings.fix: Both properties removed with an explanatory comment so they are not reintroduced.

findings.title: No skip link to bypass navigation
findings.evidence: SG-02 and SG-03 both failed at baseline.
findings.root_cause: Never implemented; the shell renders Sidebar, Topbar and content with no bypass.
findings.fix: Skip link added as the first element of the app shell, ahead of Sidebar/Topbar in source order, targeting id=main-content on a tabIndex={-1} main. Positioned fixed -top-24 -> focus:top-3 rather than sr-only/focus:not-sr-only, because both utilities set position and the winner depends on Tailwind's sort order. Click handler calls preventDefault so activation does not rewrite location.hash and break #view=<key> deep links.
findings.confidence_reason: Focus movement verified by source assertion, not by driving a browser.
findings.verification: Guard SG-02 (presence + tabIndex=-1) and SG-03 (source order)

findings.title: SPA navigation moved no focus, announced nothing, and left document.title stale
findings.evidence: SG-07 and SG-08 failed at baseline. As a hash-view SPA with no router, none of the usual route-transition hooks fired: focus stayed on the nav control, document.title never changed, and assistive tech received no feedback.
findings.root_cause: The three side effects a router normally provides were never reimplemented for the hash-view store.
findings.fix: Effect keyed on view in app-shell.tsx: (1) document.title = '${label} — StockSense', restored to the default on unmount so the login page is not labelled with the last visited view; (2) mainRef.current.focus() on a tabIndex={-1} main; (3) a persistent role=status aria-live=polite region written imperatively via textContent, since React must not manage its children or it would wipe the text on re-render.
guards: First run skipped via a prevView ref, so focus is not stolen on mount; ref-based so it survives React StrictMode's double effect invocation.

Modal guard: openProduct() switches view and opens the detail dialog in one store update (search command, scan dialog). Child effects run before parent effects, so without a guard main would yank focus out of the just-opened dialog. The effect bails when activeElement is inside — or a modal exists at all — [role=dialog][data-state=open], [role=alertdialog][data-state=open], the same selector this codebase already uses in scan-dialog.tsx.
Imperative live-region text also satisfies react-hooks/set-state-in-effect, which the original setState version violated.
findings.confidence_reason: Mechanism is source-verified; the announcement behaviour itself was not exercised with a screen reader.
findings.verification: Guard SG-07 (focus move + live announcement + modal guard) and SG-08 (document.title set on view change)

findings.title: Mobile bottom navigation conveyed current state by colour only, without aria-current
findings.evidence: SG-05 failed at baseline with 0 aria-current attributes on the bottom tab bar.
findings.root_cause: Active state expressed only through the text-primary class.
findings.fix: aria-current=page on all 4 tab controls and on both sheet item lists (6 attributes total; active items are detected rather than assumed).
findings.note: The visual state already carried a non-colour cue (font-medium + bg-primary/10 chip + indicator dot), so this was not a colour-only failure — the gap was purely semantic.

findings.title: Continuous animation not disabled under prefers-reduced-motion
findings.evidence: SG-09 failed at baseline: .animate-pulse, .animate-ping and .lift:hover kept animating under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
findings.root_cause: Reduced-motion block covered only transform/transition utilities, not the keyframe utilities.
findings.fix: All three neutralised in the reduced-motion block.
findings.deliberate_exception: animate-spin was kept on the offline-sync indicator: it is the essential status affordance, and removing it leaves a static spinner indistinguishable from a frozen one. WCAG 2.3.3 exempts essential motion.

findings.title: Fixed bottom tab bar covered the footer and last rows of every view
findings.evidence: SG-10 failed at baseline: main had pb-8 (32px) against a fixed bar of h-16 (64px) plus the iOS safe-area inset.
findings.root_cause: Clearance was applied to <main>, but the footer is the element the fixed bar actually covers, and the value was half the bar height.
findings.fix: New .bottom-nav-space class on the shell's inner column: padding-bottom: calc(4rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)), reset at min-width 48rem (Tailwind md) where the bar is hidden.
findings.verification: Guard SG-10 (applied in shell + defined with env() + reset at the md breakpoint)

findings.title: Clickable div[role=img] QR sticker unreachable by keyboard
findings.evidence: jsx-a11y/click-events-have-key-events and jsx-a11y/no-static-element-interactions on rack-grid.tsx:52: <div onClick={onClick} role=img aria-label=... title=.../>. Two independent failures: no keyboard activation path, and a role claiming to be a static image while behaving as a button.
findings.root_cause: Interactive element built from a presentational primitive.
findings.fix: Replaced with <button type=button> carrying aria-label and a focus-visible ring. QrSticker is only ever instantiated with an onClick, so a button is always correct.
findings.verification: npm run lint (extended jsx-a11y set) — finding no longer reported; npm run audit:a11y

findings.title: Count-scope radios had no reliable accessible name
findings.evidence: Radix RadioGroupItem renders <button type=button role=radio>. ARIA name computation for button takes name-from-content before any label-derived source, and this button's content was only the indicator circle — the visible 'Location / Product' text sat in sibling spans inside the <label>. The two scopes could announce as identical unnamed radios, yet the choice determines the whole count sheet.
findings.root_cause: Implicit <label> association assumed to apply to a control Radix renders as a button whose name comes from content.
findings.fix: Explicit aria-labelledby referencing both the title and description spans, making the name deterministic across browsers rather than dependent on implicit association.
findings.confidence_reason: The defect depends on browser name computation, which was not observed directly; the fix makes the outcome correct regardless.
findings.verification: npm run lint (extended jsx-a11y set) + code inspection

findings.title: Dashboard metric progressbars had no accessible name
findings.evidence: jsx-a11y/control-has-associated-label on metrics-panel.tsx:134: role=progressbar with aria-valuenow but no name, so a screen reader reported a bare percentage with no indication of what it measured.
findings.root_cause: Widget markup added without an accessible name.
findings.fix:
aria-labelledby pointing at the metric title

, with the id derived from item.key (already unique enough to serve as the React key).

findings.title: Offscreen canvas aria-hidden / control-label rule conflict
findings.evidence: The decode buffer is className=hidden (display:none), which already removes it from the a11y tree and the tab order. With aria-hidden it trips no-aria-hidden-on-focusable; without it, control-has-associated-label demands a name. jsx-a11y is CSS-unaware, so neither is a real defect.
findings.root_cause: Static lint cannot evaluate display:none.
findings.fix: Dropped aria-hidden and supplied a name, which silences both rules without changing runtime behaviour.

findings.title: A11y lint coverage extended as root-cause regression guard
findings.evidence: eslint-config-next registers only 6 jsx-a11y rules, all at warning level, covering ARIA validity and img alt — nothing about labels, keyboard interaction, focus or landmarks.
findings.root_cause: Tooling gap: the rule classes that produced UXA-014 and UXA-015 were not covered by any automated check.
findings.fix: Added 21 jsx-a11y rules to eslint.config.mjs at warning level so npm run lint still exits 0. Two options were required to keep the signal clean: label-has-associated-control needs controlComponents (Input, Textarea, Select, Switch, Checkbox, RadioGroupItem, InputOtp, Calendar, Slider) because jsx-a11y cannot resolve a custom component to the DOM control it renders; control-has-associated-label needs ignoreElements (td, th, tr) and ignoreRoles because table cells are layout, not controls.
findings.config_note: The jsx-a11y plugin is registered by nextCoreWebVitals; flat config rejects a second registration with 'Cannot redefine plugin', so the extension declares rules only.
findings.verification: npm run lint exits 0 with 3 warnings

findings.title: Clickable span with onClick is not keyboard-operable (login OTP debug affordance)
findings.deferred_to: owner of the in-flight mail/OTP work
findings.evidence: npm run lint reports jsx-a11y/click-events-have-key-events and jsx-a11y/no-static-element-interactions at login-view.tsx:527: setResetOtp(debugOtp)}>{debugOtp}
findings.root_cause: Interactive span used instead of a button.
findings.why_not_fixed: login-view.tsx carries in-flight uncommitted owner work (the mail/OTP feature). Editing it risked clobbering changes not yet written to disk.
findings.recommended_fix: Promote to <button type=button>, or add role=button, tabIndex={0} and Enter/Space handling.

findings.title: anchor-has-content reported on PaginationLink
findings.ruling: children arrives via the {...props} spread, so content exists at runtime; the rule cannot see through the spread. Not enabled in the lint config.

findings.title: control-has-associated-label reported on <td> cells
findings.ruling: Table cells are layout, not controls, and never require an accessible name. Handled by ignoreElements/ignoreRoles in the lint config.

findings.title: label-has-associated-control reported on correctly-wrapped labels
findings.ruling: jsx-a11y cannot resolve a custom component (Input, Switch, RadioGroupItem) to the DOM control it renders. Runtime names are present via aria-label, or via the aria-labelledby added by UXA-015. Handled by controlComponents in the lint config.

findings.title: 26x prefer-tag-over-role style suggestions
findings.ruling: Not enabled by default. <div role=status> is used in 9 places across the existing codebase, so changing one would be inconsistent; role=status and <output> expose the same role. <div role=dialog> -> <dialog> likewise.

findings.title: autoFocus on the search command input
findings.ruling: Focusing the query field when a Cmd+K palette opens is the established convention and matches user expectation, so it was accepted rather than changed. Noted here for SC 3.2.1 completeness. Rule not enabled in the lint config.

findings.title: Login field errors set aria-invalid but are never linked to the control
findings.deferred_to: owner of the in-flight mail/OTP work
findings.evidence:
login-view.tsx:379 and :409 set aria-invalid on the email and password inputs; the sibling error

at :383 and :413 carries no id, and neither input has aria-describedby.
findings.root_cause: Hand-rolled error rendering with no programmatic association to the control.
findings.why_not_fixed: login-view.tsx carries in-flight uncommitted owner work (the mail/OTP feature). Editing it risked clobbering changes not yet written to disk.
findings.recommended_fix:
Add an id to each error

and reference it from the input with aria-describedby, mirroring new-delivery-dialog.tsx.
findings.guard_encoding: SG-13 passes this file through its KNOWN_OPEN list and reports 'known-open finding UXA-025'; the exception clears itself the moment the link is added.

findings.title: Topbar h2 precedes the document's only h1 and repeats it verbatim
findings.deferred_to: owner of the in-flight mail work
findings.evidence: topbar.tsx:84 renders the view label as <h2>, where meta is NAV_BY_VIEW[view]. All 11 views pass that identical string as their PageHeader <h1> title, and the topbar renders before <main>, so heading order descends before it ascends and every view name is announced twice.
findings.root_cause: The view label is emitted as a heading in application chrome rather than as text.
findings.why_not_fixed: topbar.tsx carries in-flight owner work (+25 lines for the mail hub).
findings.recommended_fix:
Change the

to a

at topbar.tsx:84. Tailwind preflight resets heading size and weight to inherit, so the rendered output is identical.

findings.title: Shared FormMessage rendered validation errors with no live-region role
findings.evidence:
FormMessage returned null unless a message existed, then rendered a bare

. The node mounts at the exact moment validation fails, and inserting an element with no live-region role announces nothing; aria-describedby only surfaces the text when the field is next focused.
findings.root_cause: Conditional render with no live region, so the failure moment is silent for a screen reader.
findings.fix: role={error ? 'alert' : undefined} on the message node, so error text is announced while non-error helper text passed through props.children is not.
findings.impact: Every react-hook-form form benefits: new-product-dialog, new-receipt-dialog, supplier-form-dialog, new-count-dialog.

findings.title: Hand-rolled dialog field errors were flagged invalid but never described
findings.evidence: new-delivery-dialog.tsx (customer field and each line's quantity), new-adjustment-dialog.tsx (reason textarea and counted quantity) and new-transfer-dialog.tsx (each line's quantity) set aria-invalid while the visible message had no id and the control no aria-describedby. The counted-quantity input went invalid on decimal or negative entry with no explanatory text anywhere on screen.
findings.root_cause: Forms that bypass react-hook-form hand-roll aria-invalid and render the message as an unlinked sibling element.
findings.fix: Linked each control to its message with aria-describedby. The LineHint cases gained a stable wrapper id so the existing hint doubles as the description instead of duplicating copy, and the counted-quantity input gained the message it was missing entirely, with wording matched to whichever condition actually failed.

findings.title: Dialog-level error messages had no live region
findings.evidence: new-receipt-dialog.tsx rendered errors.lines.root and errors.lines.message below the Add line button, attached to no control; new-transfer-dialog.tsx rendered its source/destination route error the same way.
findings.root_cause: Form-level messages are not associated with any control, so with no live region no path reaches them.
findings.fix: role=alert on both. The transfer route error applies it only when the message is actually an error, so the ordinary informational route text is not announced on every keystroke.

findings.title: No table header in the app declared scope
findings.evidence: Zero <th> elements carried scope= anywhere in src. Assistive tech cannot announce which column a data cell belongs to, a real loss on the wide products, history and stock tables.
findings.root_cause: The shared TableHead component omitted scope, and 8 raw headers in the print sheet were written by hand.
findings.fix: TableHead now defaults scope to col (overridable for row headers), which covers every table built from the shared kit, plus scope=col on the 8 raw headers in count-sheet-print.tsx.

static_guards.title: App shell renders a skip link to the main region
Skip link precedes the navigation landmarks in source order
Focus indicator is not drawn at reduced opacity
Mobile bottom navigation marks the current destination
Desktop sidebar marks the current destination
View changes move focus to the new content and announce it
Document title tracks the active view
Fixed bottom tab bar does not cover page content
Table column headers declare their scope (WCAG 1.3.1)
Validation messages are announced when they appear (WCAG 4.1.3)
Field errors are described, not just flagged invalid (WCAG 1.3.1 / 3.3.1)

recommendations.action: Fix the three deferred findings when the mail/OTP work lands: the keyboard-inaccessible OTP debug span, aria-describedby on the login errors (SG-13's exception then clears itself), and the topbar h2 -> p swap (no visual change).
Add `npm run audit:a11y` to CI alongside `npm run lint` so contrast and guard regressions are caught before merge.
Promote genuinely distinct semantic colours (suggestion accept, delivery complete) to named tokens instead of raw utilities, so the guard checks them in one place.
Never simplify luminance() in scripts/audit-a11y.mjs — linearising sRGB is what makes the numbers correct; the repo's earlier audit skipped it and produced false failures.
Run a short NVDA/VoiceOver pass over navigation, one dialog and one form — this closes the single largest limitation of this report (no AT testing).
Re-run `npm run audit:a11y` after any edit to globals.css theme blocks or to the bottom nav.

limitations: No assistive-technology testing. Announcements, focus order and landmark navigation are reasoned from source, not observed.
No browser execution. Skip-link activation, focus movement, the modal focus guard and reduced-motion behaviour are source-asserted.
No user testing. No USER_STUDY, no participants, no task-success measurement.
No device or viewport matrix; responsive layout reviewed by code inspection only.
Print output (count sheet stylesheet) not rendered or verified.
Success criteria listed as unevaluated in report section 6 were not audited.

Three findings (UXA-018, UXA-025, UXA-026) remain open because their files carry in-flight owner work; each is documented with a recommended fix, and UXA-025 is encoded in the guard as a known-open exception.
Static lint cannot see computed styles; contrast beyond the 57 asserted pairs and any runtime-generated colour is not covered.
